flags.text: Paper says the linter exits 2 on 'an uncompilable pattern'. That holds only for prohibited_terms.json patterns and negation guards. For the multilingual neverInStaticCopy concepts, a concept whose alternatives fail to compile (re.error -> continue) or whose `static let X = Concept(` block the regex cannot find (concept is None -> continue) is silently dropped; exit 2 happens only when zero concepts survive. A typo in one lexicon concept removes that concept from the every-locale catalogue check while the linter still prints 'clean'. (All 12 load today.)

Paper says the prohibition guard runs on comment-stripped source so 'a comment cannot excuse a string'. strip_swift_comments uses a non-nesting non-greedy /\*.*?\*/ regex (unlike the nesting-aware literal scanner), so in `/* a /* b */ never tell the user ... */` the tail of the outer comment survives stripping and can act as a guard for a literal within the 3-line window.

Paper says the linter scans the app tree, Watch app and 'both string catalogs'. The repo has a third user-facing catalog, Emuqu/InfoPlist.xcstrings (HealthKit, microphone, speech, Bluetooth permission strings), which lies outside every scan_path (Emuqu/Sources/, EmuquWatch Watch App/, the two named catalogs) and is never linted, while the Watch InfoPlist.xcstrings is picked up by rglob.
